To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a dominant paradigm in finance is the neoclassical paradigm, which is a paradigm of the market and the firm, and which is based on a set of values and assumptions that are in conflict with sustainability.

the paradigmatic change of the financial system is a process that is still in the making, with the financial crisis of 2008 being the catalyst of the change, and that it is a process that involves a wide range of stakeholders and that is not limited to the financial system itself, but is also affecting the wider society and the environment.

the paradigm of finance has been shifting from a paradigm of finance as a tool for the maximisation of shareholder value, which has been dominant for several decades, to a paradigm of finance that is concerned with sustainability, which is a relatively new phenomenon that is currently emerging.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dominant paradigms of finance and sustainability, and the possibility of a paradigm shift in finance.
the dominant paradigm of finance and its implications for the social reality of sustainability.
the ways of understanding and organizing the finance and sustainability reality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
‘paradigm is the set of experiences, values and beliefs that affect individual’s perceptions of a reality’.
‘paradigm is a set of assumptions that define the boundaries of a field of study, the questions that are asked and the methods used to answer them’ (Hart, 2010).
a paradigm is a way of seeing the world and understanding it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are trying to understand how a new paradigm of sustainable finance is emerging, how it differs from the old paradigm of financial capitalism and how it can be used as a tool to achieve sustainable development.

the paradigm shift we have been experiencing is a shift from a dominant paradigm that has been based on the assumption that economic growth is the key to solving the problems of poverty and inequality, to a new paradigm based on the assumption of the need to address the root causes of poverty and inequality.

a ‘paradigm of sustainability’ is a new way of thinking and organising the social, economic and natural world that is more inclusive, equitable, and just, and that is based on the principles of sustainability, including ecological integrity, social justice, and economic viability.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we are living through the most profound paradigm shift of all time, which is the shift from the dominant paradigm of the past 300 years of the industrial age to the emerging paradigm of the sustainability age.
a paradigm shift in the way we organise our economy is possible.
the financial system has become a paradigm in the sense that it is the dominant thought pattern and the main organising force of our society.
